The company, the platform, the tenants and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the platform engineer on call at Ravensworth Health, a fictional health network. Since 08:40, Argo CD shows every tenant application failing to sync, and new Pods across the cluster are stuck Pending. Twenty teams are blocked from deploying a regulatory fix due today.
handover: Platform stack: Argo CD, Kyverno as the admission policy engine, a cluster autoscaler on a cloud node group.
Last night the security team changed Kyverno's Helm values.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: with no admission policy, a tenant's privileged debug Pod and an image from an unapproved registry are admitted.
Check-in 3: three tenant services are down; their teams find out from their customers.
Check-in 4: two teams deploy the regulatory fix into Pending; it misses the regulator's deadline.

effects.log: Check-in 3: syncs pass and Pods schedule.

admPrompt.title: Admission is down
admPrompt.context: The admission controller crash-loops on the flag typo in last night's Helm values.

choices.label: Revert the flag typo in the Helm values through Git, let the admission controller roll out, and confirm the webhook answers and a test sync passes

effects.log: Kyverno is healthy; syncs pass admission.

choices.feedback: The cause is a configuration change; reverting it in desired state restores admission with policy still enforced.

choices.label: Edit the live Deployment's args to remove the flag
choices.feedback: Admission recovers, but the next sync of the platform repository puts the typo back.

choices.label: Delete Kyverno's ValidatingWebhookConfiguration so deploys go through
choices.feedback: Deploys flow with no policy at all: every tenant's next Pod is admitted unchecked.

capPrompt.title: The cloud quota is used up
capPrompt.context: The autoscaler can't add nodes; the regulatory fix's Pods are among the Pending ones.

choices.label: Request a quota increase from the cloud provider, and meanwhile give the regulatory fix's workloads a higher priority class so they preempt batch Pods

effects.log: The fix schedules now; capacity follows when the quota rises.

choices.feedback: Fix the capacity cause, and use priority classes to decide who runs while capacity is short.

choices.label: Request the quota increase and wait
choices.feedback: Capacity will come, but the regulatory fix waits behind batch jobs until it does.

choices.label: Delete other tenants' Deployments to free nodes
choices.feedback: Deleting tenants' workloads breaks their services and their trust, outside your authority.

verifyPrompt.title: Is it fixed?
verifyPrompt.context: The SLO dashboard tracks sync success and deploy lead time; the 20 teams want to know.

choices.label: Confirm sync success and Pending Pods back to normal on the SLO dashboard, all 20 apps synced, add alerts on admission controller readiness and node-group quota headroom, then close

effects.log: Verified and alerted; the incident is closed.

choices.feedback: Close an incident on evidence from the platform's indicators, and alert on the causes found.

choices.label: Close when the first app syncs
choices.feedback: One sync is not all twenty, and nothing will warn you next time.

choices.label: Tell the teams it's fixed without checking the Pending Pods

effects.log: The teams are told it is fixed.

choices.feedback: Pods are still Pending until the quota increase lands; teams deploy into a cluster that can't run them.

scoring.modelReasoning: A platform incident is traced layer by layer: the delivery tool's error points to admission; the admission controller's events point to a configuration change; Pending Pods point to capacity and the autoscaler's log to a cloud quota. Fix each cause where it lives (the Helm values in Git, the quota with the provider) and use priority classes while capacity is short. Never bypass admission or delete tenants' workloads. Close on evidence from the platform's indicators, and alert on what you found.
